s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute onset of painful vision loss with extensive lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: Blurred vision and loss of vision in the left lower quadrant
Vitreous haze and optic-nerve pallor in the left eye
key_facts: 63-year-old white man
3-week history of redness of the left eye
Extensive bilateral lymphadenopathy
Blurred vision and loss of vision in the left lower quadrant
Supraorbital pain in both eyes
No fever, chills, weight loss, rash, or joint pains
Several weeks of malaise
Visual acuity 20/20 in the right eye and 20/125 in the left
Intraocular pressure 11 mm Hg in the right eye and 32 mm Hg in the left
Slit-lamp examination showed 1+ cell in the right eye, 4+ cell in the left
Gelatinous layered hypopyon with red-blood-cell layering in both eyes
Dilated exam revealed 1+ vitreous haze and optic-nerve pallor in the left eye
B-scan ultrasonography showed no retinal detachment or masses
Anterior chamber paracentesis of the left eye yielded only acellular, dense, proteinaceous material

shortlist.label: Intraocular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Painless vision loss, extensive lymphadenopathy, and gelatinous layered hypopyon

shortlist.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral eye involvement, lymphadenopathy, and granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive lymphadenopathy, vision loss, and possible CNS involvement

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral eye involvement, lymphadenopathy, and granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive lymphadenopathy, vision loss, and possible systemic involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with panuveitis, extensive bilateral lymphadenopathy, and a gelatinous layered hypopyon with red-blood-cell layering in both eyes, along with the absence of systemic symptoms such as fever, chills, and weight loss, and the presence of acellular, dense, proteinaceous material in the anterior chamber paracentesis, is highly suggestive of intraocular lymphoma.

rejected.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
rejected.why: Typically presents with granulomatous uveitis, skin, and hair changes, which are not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: Although it can cause ocular symptoms, the primary presentation is usually with neurological symptoms, which are not prominent in this case

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with granulomatous uveitis, and other systemic symptoms such as lung involvement, which are not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Too broad, intraocular lymphoma is a more specific diagnosis that better explains the patient's ocular symptoms
